annotations.rationale: This reduced-function disease expression is used adjectivally to modify the noun 'phenotype' rather than to stand alone as the disease name itself.

This noun phrase is headed by 'deficiency' and takes the specific molecular entity 'glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase ( G6PD )' as its complement; it is used as the named condition with population prevalence, so it is a specific disease mention.
This is a deficiency nominalization with a specific molecular entity complement ('G6PD') and is used in a disease-denoting causal frame ('cause G6PD deficiency').
This generic deficiency term denotes a broad class of deficiency disorders rather than one uniquely defined disease, so it fits the disease-class category.
